alerts.title: Manipur: NH-2 dug up with JCBs and blocked with burning tyres at Kangpokpi town and Motbung after Chawangkining arrests
alerts.summary: Violence erupted in Kangpokpi district on September 20 after a CRPF CoBRA unit arrested six people (Seilet, Manglen, Sathao, Lenlal, Gin and Chuchung) near Kholep village in connection with the Chawangkining violence. Protesters blocked National Highway-2 (the Imphal-Dimapur lifeline highway) at Kangpokpi town and at Motbung using burning tyres and debris, and reportedly used JCB machines to dig up sections of the road to prevent security-forces movement. Security forces fired tear gas as the crowd targeted a convoy transporting the detainees, and a Casspir armoured vehicle was partially set on fire. An emergency bandh was also declared, disrupting normal movement across the district.
alerts.impact: Critical serviceability risk — NH-2 is Manipur's principal lifeline highway to the rest of India via Nagaland; with sections physically dug up at Kangpokpi town and Motbung, hold all linehaul on this route and watch for stock-out risk at the Imphal hub. Flag Kangpokpi district LM/FM as non-serviceable for the bandh period and monitor for further escalation given the fresh detentions.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: 60 roads still blocked — Mandi (33), Kangra (10), Kullu (9) — Chailchowk-Tattapani road hit again
alerts.summary: Officials report 60 roads still blocked across Himachal Pradesh as of mid-September, with Mandi district worst hit at 33 roads, followed by Kangra (10) and Kullu (9). A fresh landslide stopped traffic for three hours on the Chailchowk-Tattapani road in Mandi, and feeder stretches toward Kullu have seen episodic slides through the month. Isolated showers are forecast for the middle hills September 20-21, keeping slope conditions unstable.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Mandi/Kangra/Kullu hill-taluka pincodes: keep buffer stock at Mandi and Kullu hubs, plan alternate routing around Chailchowk-Tattapani, and flag last-mile delays for feeder-road villages until slope conditions stabilise.

alerts.title: J&K: Doda-Bhaderwah road completely blocked at Chalnai after fresh landslide, debris-clearance underway
alerts.summary: The Doda-Bhaderwah road was completely blocked near Chalnai village after a landslide on Friday, September 19, halting vehicular movement between the two towns. Men and machinery have been pressed into service to clear debris and restore traffic; the scale of the slide had not fully been assessed as of the latest reports.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Doda-Bhaderwah corridor: hold non-essential LM/linehaul via Chalnai until the road is cleared, and route via alternate approach roads where available for Bhaderwah-side pincodes.

alerts.title: Karnataka: pre-dawn landslide buries house at Montepadavu Kodi in Dakshina Kannada, kills five of one family
alerts.summary: Heavy overnight rain triggered a landslide around 4am on September 20 at Montepadavu Kodi in coastal Karnataka's Dakshina Kannada district, collapsing a house where six members of the Poojary family were asleep; five were killed. Incessant rain has lashed the district, with landslides also affecting traffic movement in other parts of Dakshina Kannada.
alerts.impact: Serviceability watch — Dakshina Kannada coastal-hill pincodes (Montepadavu and neighbouring hamlets): flag for manual verification before LM attempts given active rescue/relief operations, and build in extra transit buffer on rain-affected approach roads district-wide.

alerts.title: Kerala: landslide buries plantation shed in Idukki's Kottakamboor-Vattavada High Ranges, kills two workers
alerts.summary: Hours of heavy monsoon rain in Idukki district's High Ranges triggered a landslide that collapsed a hillside onto a temporary farm shed at Kottakamboor, Vattavada, where plantation workers had taken shelter from the downpour; two were killed and one injured. Heavy rain has persisted for several days across the border hamlets of Vattavada, Pampadumchola and Kottakamboor, keeping soil-moisture-driven landslide risk elevated. Separately, a flash flood swept away a five-member group elsewhere in Kerala on September 20, killing two with two still missing.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Idukki High Ranges (Vattavada, Pampadumchola, Kottakamboor): flag these hamlets as high landslide-risk, hold non-essential LM movement on hill roads during active rain spells, and pre-position buffer stock at the Munnar/Idukki hub.

alerts.title: Bihar: two embankments breach in Bhagalpur's Naugachia as Kosi/Ganga floods hit 10.26 lakh people across 11 districts
alerts.summary: Roughly 15 metres of an old railway-line embankment collapsed at Baniya village (Rangra block, Naugachia) under Kosi floodwater pressure, sending water rapidly toward Sadhopur, Masudanpur, Baisi, Bhawanipur and Baniya; a second, ~10-metre breach was reported in the Brahmottar embankment at Gopalpur, also in Naugachia. The Ganga has breached all-time high-water marks at Gandhi Ghat and Pandarak, and roughly 10.26 lakh people across 11 districts (Buxar, Bhojpur, Patna, Vaishali, Samastipur, Munger, Begusarai, Katihar, Bhagalpur, Khagaria and others) have been affected; the state has deployed nearly 2,000 boats and dozens of SDRF/NDRF teams for evacuation.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — Naugachia subdivision (Baniya, Sadhopur, Masudanpur, Baisi, Bhawanipur, Gopalpur panchayats): flag non-serviceable for LM until embankment breaches are plugged and water recedes. Given Naugachia's history of unrepaired embankments, treat this as a recurring seasonal non-adherence hotspot and route Bhagalpur-hub linehaul with extra buffer through the district.

alerts.title: West Bengal: Padma erosion destroys 10 houses and a temple in Murshidabad's Radhakrishnapur overnight; fresh Ganga erosion at Malda's Gopalpur-Shantimor
alerts.summary: Padma River erosion advanced nearly 200 metres inland in a single night at Radhakrishnapur village, Murshidabad, destroying 10 houses and a temple; residents had petitioned the district magistrate for protection on September 9. In Malda, a large stretch of land near Shantimor in the Gopalpur area has been eroding into the Ganga since Tuesday, and relief-distribution complaints from erosion-hit Bilaimari prompted a state minister's visit on September 15. Officials expect erosion to continue until the end of September given fluctuating Ganga water levels; ₹3,600 crore has been allotted for anti-erosion works across Malda, Murshidabad and Nadia.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — Radhakrishnapur (Murshidabad) and Gopalpur/Shantimor/Bilaimari (Malda, Ratua-I/English Bazar belt): flag these hamlets non-serviceable as addresses become invalid with active home loss; recommend manual verification calls before LM attempts and route via Malda town/Murshidabad hubs with extra buffer through end-September.

alerts.title: Bay of Bengal deep depression (possible Cyclone Arnab) to cross north AP-south Odisha coast Sep 23; red alert for Kandhamal, Gajapati, Ganjam, Puri
alerts.summary: A low-pressure system over the Andaman Sea is set to intensify into a depression on September 21 and a deep depression by September 22-23, tracking west-northwestwards to reach the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast around the morning of September 23 (potentially becoming Cyclone Arnab, the season's first). IMD has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall (20cm+) in Odisha's Kandhamal, Gajapati, Ganjam and Puri districts on September 23, with squally winds of 55-65 kmph along the south Odisha-north AP coast September 23-24. AP and Telangana are separately under orange/yellow alert September 19-24 across North Coastal AP (Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, East Godavari, Kakinada, Krishna, NTR, Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam) and interior districts (Kurnool, Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya). Fishermen are advised off the Andhra-Odisha-Bengal coast through September 24.
alerts.impact: Pre-position for landfall — Ganjam/Puri/Gajapati/Kandhamal (Odisha) and north coastal AP hubs: pre-build 3-4 day buffer stock, suspend fishing-belt LM attempts, and prepare to flag NS for low-lying coastal pincodes from September 22. Telangana/AP interior hubs (Kurnool, Anantapur, Guntur belt) should watch for waterlogging-linked delays through September 24.

alerts.title: Nagaland: Longleng cut off again as NH-702 landslide between Changtongya and Longleng stays only partly restored
alerts.summary: A major landslide on the night of September 11-12 completely obstructed the Changtongya-Longleng Road (NH-702) between chainage 5+785 and 6+050, cutting off heavy-vehicle movement to Longleng district headquarters. NHIDCL and contractor Nithin Sai Construction have been carrying out continuous debris clearance since, with light vehicles diverted via the Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong road; local reports describe Longleng as being repeatedly cut off through the monsoon.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Longleng district: hold heavy-vehicle linehaul on NH-702, route light-parcel movement via the Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong diversion, and keep buffer stock at the Changtongya gateway given the recurring nature of this closure.

alerts.title: Mizoram: landslide hits buildings in Vairengte, Kolasib district, kills 14-year-old boy amid NE-wide heavy-rain spell
alerts.summary: A rain-triggered landslide struck buildings in Vairengte town, Kolasib district, on September 12, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring at least four others. IMD had issued a regional heavy-rain warning for Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura for September 12 with thunderstorms, lightning and squally winds, and the northeastern states remain under a prolonged monsoon spell.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Vairengte and other Kolasib-belt hill settlements: flag as landslide-risk during active rain spells, hold non-essential LM movement on hill-slope approach roads, and verify addresses in slide-prone pockets before dispatch.

alerts.title: Petrol/diesel largely steady Sep 21 as crude nears $102 on Strait of Hormuz disruption; commercial LPG holds at second straight monthly hike
alerts.summary: Retail fuel prices were largely steady on September 21 — Delhi petrol ₹101.96/litre, diesel ₹95.44/litre (up 24 paise) — even as crude oil edged toward $102/barrel amid Strait of Hormuz disruption concerns. Commercial 19kg LPG cylinders remain at ₹2,747.50 in Delhi following the ₹9.50-11.50 hike effective September 1 (the second straight monthly increase), while domestic 14.2kg LPG (₹942 in Delhi) and CNG/PNG rates are unchanged.
alerts.impact: Cost watch, no action yet: no immediate LM/FM disruption, but sustained Strait of Hormuz risk and crude near $102 raise the chance of a fuel-surcharge ask from Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees if crude holds above $100 for an extended period — track daily and flag early to network-cost teams.
